extracted.intended_audience: survivors of school sexual assault and their families seeking legal representation
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and pursuing civil claims against K-12 schools and colleges/universities for sexual assault and institutional failures (including Title IX violations), and selecting appropriate counsel to hold institutions accountable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of institutional cover-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools have a system for burying the truth; institutions (and their lawyers/crisis teams) are experts at silencing victims, denying responsibility, and hiding evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for signs that administrators dismissed complaints, destroyed or concealed evidence, used crisis teams to silence victims, or otherwise took steps to protect the institution's reputation instead of investigating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of institutional liability (K-12 and higher ed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perpetrators and the negligent institutions that enable them must be held responsible, whether the abuse occurred in a K-12 school or on a university campus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims can be brought across educational levels; evaluate whether the institution had duties (hiring, supervision, security, Title IX compliance) relevant to the victim's environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for abuse by teachers, coaches, and staff
rubrics_metrics.description: When a person in authority abuses a student, the school can be held directly liable for failures in hiring, supervision, and its moral duty to protect the child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate hiring/background-check failures, ignored complaints against staff, inadequate supervision or policies allowing a staff member access to students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for assault by another student
rubrics_metrics.description: A school can be liable if it knew or should have known about a threat and failed to take reasonable action, or if it fostered a hostile environment that allowed the assault to occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess prior reports/warnings about the assailant, the school's response (or lack thereof), and whether the environment facilitated the assault.

rubrics_metrics.name: Campus-specific failures (colleges & universities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions of higher education may be accountable for Title IX failures, poor security, and ignored warning signs leading to sexual assault in dorms, fraternities, and on campus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine campus security policies, fraternity/sorority oversight, housing supervision, and the institution's compliance with Title IX procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negligent hiring and supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools failing to perform adequate background checks or ignoring complaints made against teachers, trainers, and coaches can be held liable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document absent or insufficient background checks, repeated complaints against the same individual, or failure to act on warning signs in personnel files and hiring records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ignoring reports and warnings
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear evidence that students, parents, or staff reported concerns about a perpetrator that were deliberately dismissed or covered up by administrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect records/emails/complaints showing reports were made and track administrator responses that minimized, dismissed, or concealed those reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to report to authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions illegally concealing incidents of sexual abuse from law enforcement to avoid scandal and protect their public image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether mandatory reporting duties were ignored and whether incidents were concealed from police or child-protective services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Colleges and universities failing to follow federal law in responding to claims of sexual assault, thereby creating a dangerous environment for students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the institution followed Title IX procedures (investigation, interim measures, equitable process) and whether the response was prompt and effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal standard for school liability: knowledge and reasonable action
rubrics_metrics.description: "Knew or should have known" about a threat and "failed to take reasonable action" — or created/fostered a hostile environment — as bases for legal responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish actual or constructive knowledge through prior reports, communications, patterns of misconduct, and then show that the school's response fell below reasonable standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of waivers or settlements signed under duress
rubrics_metrics.description: Any agreement or waiver the institution offered may be invalid, especially if it was signed under duress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have counsel review signed documents for signs of coercion, undue pressure, or unconscionability to determine enforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of client privacy and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Firms should take every available legal measure to protect the confidentiality of clients and shield their identities from public disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the attorney's use of protective orders, sealed filings, pseudonyms, redaction practices, and other strategies to maintain client privacy throughout the legal process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth and scope of investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations must go far beyond the perpetrator to uncover systemic negligence and deliberate choices that allowed the abuse to happen and continue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for investigation activities that include institutional records review, personnel files, pattern-of-conduct analyses, institutional policies, and communications showing deliberate choices or neglect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience and specialization of legal team
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer national trial attorneys who have built a reputation on litigating and winning complex sexual assault lawsuits against powerful educational institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate counsel's track record in similar cases, presence of specialized trial experience, and demonstrated history of holding institutions accountable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trauma-informed, client-centered representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal representation should be strategic and trauma-informed, providing compassion and ensuring the client feels safe, heard, and supported while pursuing aggressive litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the firm emphasizes trauma-informed practices, offers supportive staff, and balances compassionate client care with assertive legal strategy.
